q: 201. While designing an air entrained concrete
options: an allowance for the entrained air is made
strength of the concretes, is reduced
explain: In air-entrained concrete mix design, a specific allowance/adjustment is made in the mix proportions to account for the volume of entrained air voids introduced into the mix.

q: 202. An ideal ware house, is provided
options: 15cm thick concrete floor laid on a dry course of soling
explain: An ideal cement warehouse must have all these features together - waterproof walls and roof, few closed windows, and a proper concrete floor on dry soling - to protect stored cement from moisture.

q: 203. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: space between the exterior walls of a ware house and bag piles should be 30 cm
cement bags should preferably be piled on wooden planks
cement bags should be placed such that bags of one layer does not touch the bags of the adjacent layer
width and height of the pile should not exceed 3 m and 2.70 m respectively
explain: All four statements (a-d) describe correct, standard warehouse storage practices for cement bags, so 'none of the above' (i.e., all are correct) is the right answer.

q: 204. The specification of a cement bag for storage, are
explain: A standard cement bag has all these specifications together - 50 kg weight, about 18 cm height, roughly 3000 sq.cm plan area, and about 35 litres volume.

q: 205. Ware house pack of cement means
options: pressure exertion of the bags of upper layers
pressure compaction of bags on lower layers
explain: 'Warehouse pack' refers to the compaction/packing effect experienced by the lower bags due to the pressure exerted by the weight of bags stacked above them.

q: 206. Ware house set cement is
options: cement which absorbs moisture in ware house
cement which sets due to being adjacent wall
cement which gets compressed due to load of several bags above it
explain: 'Warehouse set' cement refers to cement that has been compacted/hardened somewhat due to the pressure of the load of many bags stacked above it during storage, not due to hydration.

q: 207. If the effective plan area of a warehouse is 54sq.m, and maximum height of piles permitted is 270cm, the number of cement bags to be stored, is
explain: Using standard warehouse storage calculations (based on typical bag dimensions and stacking density), a plan area of 54 sq.m with a pile height of 2.70 m works out to approximately 2700 bags of cement that can be stored.

q: 208. The internal dimensions of a ware house are 15m x 5.6m, and the maximum height of piles is 2.70 m. The maximum number of bags to be stored in two piles, are
explain: Based on the given warehouse dimensions (15m x 5.6m) with a maximum stacking height of 2.70 m, divided into two piles, the calculated maximum storage capacity works out to 3000 bags.

q: 209. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: with passage of time, the strength of cement increases
with passage of time, the strength of cement decreases
after a period of 24 months, the strength of cement reduces to 50 %
The concrete made with storage deteriorated cement, gains strength with time
explain: Cement strength actually decreases (not increases) over prolonged storage time due to gradual absorption of atmospheric moisture and partial hydration, making statement (a) incorrect.

q: 210. To ensure constant moisture content in aggregates
options: area of each aggregate pile should be large
height of each aggregate pile should not exceed 1.50 m
aggregate pile should be left for 24 hours before aggregates are used
conical heaps of aggregates should be avoided to prevent moisture vibration
explain: All these storage practices together - larger pile area, limited height, resting period, and avoiding conical heaps - help maintain a uniform and constant moisture content in stockpiled aggregates.

q: 211. An aggregate which passes through 25mm IS sieve and is retained on 20mm sieve, is said to be flaky if its least dimension is less than
explain: As per the flakiness index definition, an aggregate passing a 25mm sieve and retained on a 20mm sieve is classified as flaky if its least dimension (thickness) is less than 13.5 mm (0.6 times the mean sieve size).

q: 212. Workability of concrete for a given water content is good if aggregates used, are
explain: Rounded aggregates have lower surface area and less interlocking friction, resulting in better workability for a given water content compared to angular, irregular, or flaky aggregates.

q: 213. An excess of flaky particles in concrete aggregates
options: increase the quantity of water and sand
explain: Excess flaky particles negatively affect concrete in all these ways - reducing workability, increasing water/sand demand, harming durability - and hence limits (like 15% maximum) are specified.

q: 214. Grading of sand causes great variation in
explain: The grading (particle size distribution) of sand significantly influences all these aspects of concrete - its workability, strength, durability, and ease of handling/placing.

q: 215. The durability of concrete is due to its resistance to
explain: Durability of concrete is defined by its overall ability to resist deterioration from a combination of environmental exposure, internal disruptive forces, and chemical attack/cracking.

q: 216. The inelastic behavior of concrete is due to the
options: propagation of bond and mortar cracks
presence of macro and micro cracks
explain: The inelastic (non-linear stress-strain) behaviour of concrete is primarily attributed to the progressive propagation of bond cracks (at aggregate-paste interface) and mortar cracks under loading.

q: 217. The modulus of elasticity of concrete improves with
explain: As concrete matures/ages, continued hydration increases its density and strength, which in turn improves (increases) its modulus of elasticity.

q: 218. Which of the following does not react with concrete?
explain: Alcohol is generally chemically inert with respect to hardened concrete and does not cause any significant chemical reaction or deterioration, unlike sewage water, sulphuric acid, or vegetable oil.

q: 219. The presence of algae in concrete
options: causes a large entrainment of air
explain: Algae contamination in concrete negatively affects it in multiple ways - reducing strength, weakening bond between paste and aggregate, and causing excessive air entrainment.

q: 220. Quality control means
options: a rational use of available resources
explain: Quality control fundamentally refers to the rational and efficient use of available resources (materials, labour, equipment) to consistently achieve the desired quality standards.

q: 221. The cube strength of concrete exceeds the cylinder strength by (in percent)
explain: Due to the difference in specimen geometry and the resulting confinement/end effects during testing, cube strength typically exceeds cylinder strength by about 20 to 25%.

q: 222. For cylindrical specimens, the dimension of cylinder generally used
explain: The standard cylindrical test specimen used for compressive strength testing has a diameter of 15 cm and a height of 30 cm, giving the standard height-to-diameter ratio of 2.

q: 223. For cylindrical specimens, minimum strength required should be
options: 0.20 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
0.40 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
0.60 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
0.80 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
explain: The compressive strength obtained from a standard cylinder is typically about 0.80 times the strength of an equivalent 15 cm cube, due to the difference in specimen shape and testing conditions.

q: 224. The surface area of standard cube used for finding compressive strength of concrete is
explain: The standard cube face is 15cm x 15cm = 225 cm² = 22500 mm² = 0.0225 m² - all these are equivalent expressions of the same area in different units, so all of the above is correct.

q: 225. During application of load on cylindrical specimen the failure plane makes an angle of .........with the horizontal.
explain: Under compressive load, cylindrical concrete specimens typically fail along a shear plane inclined at approximately 60 degrees to the horizontal (or about 30 degrees to the vertical axis of loading).

q: 226. For given water content, workability decreases if the concrete aggregates contain an excess of
explain: Excess of thin, flat, elongated, or flaky particles all increase surface area and interlocking, reducing workability of concrete for a given water content, so all of these are correct.

q: 227. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: according to the petrological characteristics, concrete aggregates are classified as heavy weight, normal weight and light weight
according to the shape of the particles, concrete aggregates are classified as rounded, irregular, angular and flaky
according to the surface texture of the particles, the concrete aggregates are classified as glossy, smooth, granular, rough, crystalline, honey combed and porous
explain: Aggregates can indeed be classified in all three ways simultaneously - by petrological characteristics (weight), by particle shape, and by surface texture - making all statements correct.

q: 228. Water in excess of that required for chemical reaction in concrete results in
explain: Excess water beyond what's chemically required for hydration tends to rise to the surface of freshly placed concrete, a phenomenon known as bleeding.

q: 229. Saw dust can be rendered chemically inert by boiling it in water containing
explain: Boiling saw dust in a solution containing ferrous sulphate neutralizes its harmful sugars/tannins, rendering it chemically inert so it can be safely used in concrete or lightweight products.

q: 230. For given workability the grading requiring the least amount of water is one that gives
options: greatest surface area for the given cement and aggregates
least surface area for the given cement and aggregates
lest weight for the given cement and aggregates
greatest weight for the given cement and aggregates
explain: A grading that produces the least surface area of aggregate particles (for a given volume) requires the least amount of water to wet and coat the surfaces, achieving the desired workability with minimum water.

q: 231. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: 5% of the total aggregates for low workability with a coarse grading
10% of the total aggregates for low workability with a coarse grading
20% of the total aggregates for a mix having high workability with fine grading
explain: These percentages represent standard recommended proportions of fines depending on the required workability and grading type, so all the given statements are correct together.

q: 232. Pozzolanic properties exist in
explain: All these materials - shales, fly ash, pumicite, and diatomaceous clay - are known to possess pozzolanic properties, meaning they can react with calcium hydroxide to form cementitious compounds.

q: 233. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
explain: Using a well-graded aggregate (a proper mix of various particle sizes) ensures minimum voids, better packing, and hence better quality and durability of concrete.

q: 234. Ordinary portland cement is manufactured from
explain: as per book b .Ordinary Portland Cement is primarily manufactured from limestone (calcareous material) and clay (argillaceous material) as the main raw materials.

q: 235. Allowable shear strength of concrete, depends upon
explain: The allowable shear strength of concrete is generally derived as a function of, and depends upon, its compressive strength, as per design code provisions.

q: 236. The strength of concrete is decreased by
explain: Excessive vibration (over-vibration), impact loading, and fatigue (repeated cyclic loading) can all contribute to a decrease in the effective strength of concrete over time.

q: 237. The most appropriate method to specify the concrete mix is by
explain: Specifying concrete by its grade (e.g., M20, M25) is considered the most appropriate and standardized method, as it directly denotes the required characteristic compressive strength.

q: 238. The total number of grades of ordinary concrete stipulated in IS 456:2000 are
explain: IS 456:2000 stipulates a total of 6 grades under the ordinary concrete category (M10, M15, M20, M25, M30... within the ordinary grade group).

q: 239. The standard size of a concrete cube for compressive strength test is
explain: The standard concrete cube specimen size used for compressive strength testing is 150 mm x 150 mm x 150 mm (15 cm cube).

q: 240. If the various concrete ingredients i.e. cement, sand and aggregates are in the ratio of 1:3:6, the grade of concrete, is
explain: The nominal mix ratio 1:3:6 corresponds to the M150 grade of concrete as per standard grade-mix ratio correlations.

q: 241. Permissible compressive strength of M150 concrete grade is
explain: As indicated by its designation, the M150 grade of concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 150 kg/cm².

q: 242. Permissible compressive strength of M150 concrete grade is
explain: 150 kg/cm² is equivalent to approximately 15 N/mm² (since 1 N/mm² ≈ 10.2 kg/cm²), making 15 N/mm² the correct equivalent expression of the M150 grade strength.

q: 243. Permissible compressive strength of M200 concrete grade is
explain: By definition, the M200 grade concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 200 kg/cm².

q: 244. The ratio of various ingredients (cement, sand, aggregates) in concrete of grade M 200, is
explain: The M200 grade of concrete typically corresponds to a nominal mix ratio of 1:1.5:3 (cement:sand:aggregate).

q: 245. Permissible compressive strength of M250 concrete grade is
explain: By definition, the M250 grade concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 250 kg/cm².

q: 246. Permissible compressive strength of M300 concrete grade is
explain: By definition, the M300 grade concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 300 kg/cm².

q: 247. Internal friction between the ingredients of concrete, is decreased by using
explain: Using more water (which lubricates the mix) along with coarse aggregate (which has less surface area/friction compared to fine material) reduces the internal friction between the concrete ingredients.

q: 248. Le-Chatelier's apparatus is used for testing
explain: Le-Chatelier's apparatus is a standard test device specifically used to determine the soundness of cement, i.e., its tendency to undergo volume expansion after setting.

q: 249. Slump test is done for
explain: The slump test is a standard test performed specifically to measure the workability/consistency of fresh concrete, not clay, sand, or lime.

q: 250. Workability of concrete may be improved by adding
explain: All these admixtures/materials - fly ash, hydrated lime, calcium chloride, and bentonite - are known to improve the workability of concrete mixes when added in appropriate quantities.
